summary: A TMS Software blog post by Bernard (dated Friday, March 29, 2024) introduces PDFSignVerify, a proof-of-concept application for signing and verifying PDF documents with PKCS#11 tokens. It builds on an earlier post about token-based signing and explains the ETSI-based approach using the ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute, since TMS Cryptography Pack does not support SHA1 for new signatures. The post notes successful interoperability tests with several PDF readers and that the tool is free to use.
one_line: TMS Software blog post introducing PDFSignVerify, a free proof-of-concept tool for signing and verifying PDFs with PKCS#11 tokens.
key_facts: The blog post was dated Friday, March 29, 2024 and is titled 'Signing and verifying PDF documents with TMS Cryptography Pack'.
PDFSignVerify is described as a proof of concept (PoC) application for signing and verifying PDFs with PKCS#11 tokens.
The PoC is limited because it is not possible to address all PDF versions and formats in a simple tool.
PDF specifications are laid out in an ISO standard, cited as ISO 32000-2:2020.
PDF signatures are added as Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) sequences coded in ASN.1 DER.
PDFSignVerify uses the ETSI EN 319 141-1 and 141-2 standards.
TMS Cryptography Pack does not support SHA1 for new signatures, so the PoC uses the ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute in the Signed Attribute sequence.
The signature is applied to the ASN.1 encoding of the entire Signed Attribute sequence and added to the CMS sequence along with the message digest of the initial PDF file.
The PoC app has Sign and Verify buttons, usable once the PKCS#11 driver, token password and file have been selected.
PDFSignVerify was developed with TMS Cryptography Pack version 5.0, which the post says will be issued in a few weeks.
Version 5.0 is fully written in Pascal Object and removes deprecated algorithms such as RIPEMD160.
The new PDF signatures were successfully tested for interoperability with Adobe Acrobat Reader, FoxIT PDF Reader, PDF X-Change Editor and Microsoft Edge.
PDFSignVerify is free of use and can be downloaded from download.tmssoftware.com.
The previous blog post discussed signing documents with tokens and proposed a simple tool to check the content of a PKCS#11 token.
